newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico to keep soybean meal import tariff - ASA.
newsitem.headline: Mexico to keep soybean meal import tariff - ASA.

text.p: The Mexican government is unlikely to change a current 10.5 percent tariff on imports of soybean meal, the local office of the American Soybean Association (ASA) said Tuesday.

"Efforts to persuade the government to reduce import tariffs on soybean meal have not progressed," the ASA said in an update. "The 10.5 percent tariff will be in effect for the rest of this year and we can consider this subject closed permanently," it added.
Soybean meal buyers have been fighting to have the tariffs wiped out or at least reduced to cut costs for months in closed door meetings with officials from the Trade and Agriculture Ministries.
National soybean and other oilseed crushers, however, have fought to keep the tariffs in place to protect their domestic markets from a flood of imports.
--Chris Aspin, Mexico City newsroom (525) 7289530. E-mail at chris.aspin@reuters.com
